v2_changes_summary: cluster_self_cooldown: 14 trading days post-emission; each (ticker, cluster_date) key suppresses re-entry for 14 trading days; reduces trade count from v1 ~1137 to v2 182

frequency_based_stage2_classifier: replaces dormant calendar-quarter bucketing with rolling-12-month sale count per insider; routine threshold = 4 sales/year within window; designed to make Stage 2 discriminate where the quarterly approach could not

implementation_notes.patch_description: aux_data_loader projects role + shares_owned_after (carried over from v1 fix at commit 096aaf7). Both v2 changes (cooldown + frequency classifier) added on this branch at commits 53d33f2 + 23d551b.

baseline_a.notes: Matches v1 baseline byte-for-byte: Sharpe 14.1305 / 9 trades / MaxDD 1.16%. Confirms v2 branch does not perturb S12.

modified_s15_standalone.description: S15 alone (OpportunisticInsiderShort) with frequency classifier ON and 14d cooldown, OPENCLAW_S15_INSIDER_OPPORTUNISTIC=1, OPENCLAW_S12_SELL_CLUSTER=0
modified_s15_standalone.notes: Cooldown reduced trade count from 1137→182 (84% reduction). However Sharpe went from +0.14 (v1) to -1.60 (v2) — negative and worsened. The 14d cooldown appears to have selected a worse-performing subset: the clusters that are NOT on cooldown (i.e., first occurrence or post-cooldown) have a more negative avg_pnl (-0.383%) than the full v1 pool (-0.245%). Return also flipped from +3.88% to -0.58%. The short signal itself appears to have negative edge when the cooldown logic selects for fresh clusters.

ablation.description: S15 with Stage 2 frequency classifier DISABLED (OPENCLAW_S15_DISABLE_OPPORTUNISTIC_CLASSIFIER=1) — every cluster seller treated as opportunistic
ablation.notes: IDENTICAL to modified_s15_standalone — same trade count (182), same Sharpe (-1.597), same MaxDD (9.37%), byte-for-byte identical exit breakdown. The frequency-based Stage 2 classifier is still non-discriminating on the current insider parquet, for the same structural reason as v1: insufficient density of per-insider rolling sales history to hit the 4/year threshold for 'routine' classification. See ablation_root_cause_analysis.

ablation_root_cause_analysis.finding: Frequency classifier is non-discriminating. Identical to v1 ablation outcome.
ablation_root_cause_analysis.mechanism: classify_insider() with the new frequency model windows the rolling 12 months prior to each bar date. For bars in the 2025-11-28 → 2026-05-28 window, this means the classifier inspects roughly Dec 2024 → May 2026. The insider parquet has insufficient S-Sale event density per individual insider (most appear once or twice in any 12-month window) to reach the 4-sale/year 'routine' threshold. Empirically: the vast majority of (ticker, insider_name) pairs have ≤2 sales in any 12-month slice of the parquet. The frequency model is a better-designed gate than the calendar-quarter approach, but still needs ≥3-4 years of per-insider sale history to discriminate reliably.
ablation_root_cause_analysis.code_correctness: The frequency classifier logic is correctly implemented and the ablation env var is correctly read. This is a DATA depth property, not a code defect — the same conclusion as v1.
ablation_root_cause_analysis.new_vs_v1: v1 root cause: ≥3 distinct calendar quarters per insider (quarterly bucketing); v2 root cause: ≥4 S-Sale events in rolling 12 months (frequency model). Both gates require historical depth the current parquet cannot yet provide.
ablation_root_cause_analysis.remediation: Data accumulation path: the insider parquet grows organically as each weekly pipeline run adds new rows. The frequency classifier will begin discriminating when per-insider sale counts within rolling 12-month windows reach the threshold — approximately 1-2 years of continued operation. No code change needed; the design is correct.

modified_combined.description: Portfolio-level Sharpe computed from the union of S12 BUY trades (run_id 385a763f) + S15 SHORT trades (run_id 52bd6dd6), using equal-weighted daily portfolio methodology matching aggregate_metrics() in unified_backtest.py
modified_combined.methodology_note: Built daily_pnls dict from both run_ids' strategy_backtest_trades, distributed pnl_pct evenly across holding_days, equal-weighted on each day. Sharpe annualized by sqrt(252), risk-free = 5%/252. Identical to aggregate_metrics() implementation.

standalone.result: Cooldown reduced trades 84% but Sharpe flipped negative; v2 is WORSE than v1 standalone

combined.result: Combined Sharpe went from marginally positive (0.18) to deeply negative (-1.21); v2 combined is decisively worse

computed_suggestion_rationale: Four of six acceptance gates fail; v2 is decisively worse than v1 on every performance metric. The cluster self-cooldown (v2's primary change) reduced trade count from 1,137 to 182 as expected, but produced a negative outcome: Sharpe went from +0.14 (v1) to -1.60 (v2), and return flipped from +3.88% to -0.58%. This indicates that the clusters firing on first occurrence (before the 14d cooldown suppresses them) have negative edge — the v1 trades that occurred on re-signals within 14 days of the original cluster were the ones carrying positive PnL. By eliminating them, the cooldown has removed the signal entirely. The combined portfolio Sharpe of -1.21 collapses the S12 baseline (14.13 → -1.21) and MaxDD exceeds the 8% cap (8.53%). The frequency-based Stage 2 classifier, while better-designed than the v1 quarterly approach, remains inert on the current insider parquet for the same structural reason: insufficient per-insider sale history depth to hit the 4/year threshold. Ablation remains byte-identical to standalone. HOLD rationale: The v2 design changes have negative empirical impact; the strategy should not be deployed in its current v2 form. The cooldown hypothesis (that first-occurrence clusters are better quality) is falsified by this backtest — the opposite appears true. Next investigation: (a) Consider removing or relaxing the cooldown entirely; (b) examine whether the re-signal pattern within 14d of emission is the actual alpha source; (c) probe per-cluster PnL to identify whether any signal sub-class has positive edge; (d) the frequency classifier design is sound — defer judgment on it until data depth increases.
